title: Are Superpages Super-fast? Distilling Flash Blocks to Unify Flash Pages of a Superpage in an SSD
problem: Process variation causes individual flash pages within superpages to have different read/write performance, degrading overall SSD performance when slow and fast pages are grouped together.
motivation: Improving flash superpage organization directly enhances SSD performance, which is critical for modern computer systems.
method: The paper characterizes flash memory chips to identify performance variations in individual pages, then develops a Process Variation Check (PV Check) scheme that profiles page performance at runtime and groups matched pages into superpages to minimize performance heterogeneity impact.
key_novelty: Runtime characterization-based dynamic superpage formation that groups flash pages by performance to mitigate process variation effects.
contributions: Empirical proof of performance heterogeneity within flash superpages due to process variation
Flash memory characterization methodology for identifying individual page performance variations
PV Check scheme for runtime optimization of superpage formation with low overhead
16.61% program latency and 34.55% erase latency improvement versus traditional methods

metrics.speedup: 16.61% program latency reduction, 34.55% erase latency reduction
